findings.problem: The hint 'on top of, over' leads straight to 'encima de' (and in Latin America 'arriba de'), which are common, correct answers for 'the keys on top of the table', so sobre is not the only right answer.
findings.fix: hint: one-word preposition meaning on top of; not en

back.es: on, on top of, over (preposition); also about
back.example: I left the keys on the table.

note: The trick is accurate: sobre comes from Latin super, which means above or over.
